segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.

and [a measure] of barley for two thousand and forty [zuzas];
and many perished from famine.
And in the year 376
of the Arabs [986/987 AD],
when the Caliph al-Ta'i' sat upon his throne during their festival,
and Samsam al-Dawla the ruler entered to greet him,
and he kissed the ground and stood at the right side of the throne.
And all the grandees also entered and did likewise.
And poets also entered,
and more than all the grandees, they praised Samsam [al-Dawla] in their poems.
Then, while they were feeling this [envy],
one of the grandees, named Sharaf al-Dawla, forged a conspiracy with the rest of the grandees,
and they seized Samsam al-Dawla secretly,
and sent and imprisoned him in one of the fortified cities of Persia, and they also blinded him {kohl-needled him}.
And that Sharaf al-Dawla took his place.
In these times, the kings of the Arabs—that is, the caliphs—possessed only the name and the proclamation [in the khutba];
rather, all the authority, the armies, and the treasury were managed by the hand of these Persian grandees.
And in the year 378
[378 AH, 988/989 AD], Sharaf al-Dawla gathered the philosophers who were in the domain of the Arabs,
and built a tower {observatory} for observing the movements of the stars.
And he prepared instruments of observation and copper circles,
just as al-Ma'mun had also done in his days.
And he appointed Abu Sahl Wayjan ibn Rustam al-Quhi {Guraya} over the work.
And in this year, in Tammuz [July] and in Ab [August],
hot scorching winds blew from the south,
and many fell in the streets and died suddenly in Baghdad,
especially the sailors upon the rivers of Babylon.
And in the year 379
of the Arabs [989/990 AD], Sharaf al-Dawla died,
and Abu Nasr succeeded him as head of the armies.
And in the year 380
of the Arabs [990/991 AD],
when al-Aziz, the caliph of Egypt, also gained dominion over all Syria,
he made a certain man from the Egyptian Christians his grand procurator,
whose name was Isa bar Nestorius.
And he was an eminent man and skilled in the art of the nomikoi [scribal administration/finance],
and he gathered great wealth for the royal treasury.
And he also appointed another nomikos in Syria, a Jew,
whose name was Menasseh bar Qazzaz {OCR?}; and both of these dismissed the Arab nomikoi,
and appointed Christians and Jews in their place.
